world.title: US and Cuban envoys clash as UN prepares embargo vote
world.summary: A shouting match between U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz and Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez briefly halted General Assembly debate Tuesday on a resolution calling for an end to Washington’s decades-old embargo on Cuba. Rodríguez called Waltz a liar after the U.S. envoy criticized Cuba’s governm
world.content: A shouting match between U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz and Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez briefly halted General Assembly debate Tuesday on a resolution calling for an end to Washington’s decades-old embargo on Cuba. Rodríguez called Waltz a liar after the U.S. envoy criticized Cuba’s government; Waltz told the Cuban delegation to back away from the podium. The session chair paused proceedings, then allowed Waltz to resume. President Donald Trump’s administration intensified pressure on Havana through restrictions on oil shipments and a threat to impose tariffs on countries supplying Cuba with fuel. The Associated Press reported that the oil measures have contributed to widespread power cuts affecting cooking, water supplies and communications on the island. The annual non-binding resolution was expected to come to a vote Wednesday, Oct. 28. Washington urged member states to oppose it, while Cuba sought support for ending the embargo.
world.image_alt: US and Cuban envoys clash as UN prepares embargo vote

world.title: US health chief falsely denies Arab achievements, drawing backlash before vote
world.summary: U.S. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. drew condemnation after saying at a Republican campaign rally in Grand Rapids, Michigan, on Oct. 26 that Arabs do not produce science or literature and have not won major international prizes. He made the remarks while campaigning for Republican Senate cand
world.content: U.S. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. drew condemnation after saying at a Republican campaign rally in Grand Rapids, Michigan, on Oct. 26 that Arabs do not produce science or literature and have not won major international prizes. He made the remarks while campaigning for Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers, who is challenging Democrat Abdul El-Sayed. Award records contradict the claims: Egyptian chemist Ahmed Zewail won the 1999 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, Jordan-born Palestinian-American chemist Omar Yaghi shared the 2025 prize, and Egyptian novelist Naguib Mahfouz won the 1988 Nobel Prize in Literature. Kennedy also blamed the Muslim Brotherhood, an Islamist political movement, for what he called stagnant Arab societies. Critics said his broad claims erase Arab achievements and could fuel anti-Arab and anti-Muslim hostility. Michigan voters are due to cast ballots in the Senate race on Nov. 3. At a Detroit appearance the day after the rally, Kennedy declined to address his comments while promoting a federal grant program for homeless people with serious mental illness or substance-use disorders.
world.image_alt: US health chief falsely denies Arab achievements, drawing backlash before vote

world.title: Lancet researchers urge global health emergency declaration for climate change
world.summary: A Lancet report by 146 researchers from 30 countries calls for climate change to be declared a global health emergency and estimates that heat caused nearly 3 million deaths worldwide from 2016 to 2023. In 2023 alone, heat was linked to a record 710,000 deaths, more than two-thirds of them attributed to human-caused cl
world.content: A Lancet report by 146 researchers from 30 countries calls for climate change to be declared a global health emergency and estimates that heat caused nearly 3 million deaths worldwide from 2016 to 2023. In 2023 alone, heat was linked to a record 710,000 deaths, more than two-thirds of them attributed to human-caused climate change, the report said. The researchers say rising temperatures have also cost the global economy more than $1 trillion a year over the past three years, while fossil fuels still supply about 80% of the world’s energy. They propose a coordinated international mechanism involving the World Health Organization and United Nations to share information, monitor threats and fund sustained responses. The report was published ahead of the COP31 climate conference, scheduled for Nov. 9-20.
world.image_alt: Lancet researchers urge global health emergency declaration for climate change

world.title: Egyptian court orders independent outlet Mada Masr closed, fines editor
world.summary: An Egyptian court on Oct. 27 ordered independent news site Mada Masr closed and fined its editor-in-chief, Lina Attalah, 3 million Egyptian pounds, the maximum penalty for operating a website without a licence. Security officers detained Attalah for several hours and released her after the outlet paid the fine. The cou
world.content: An Egyptian court on Oct. 27 ordered independent news site Mada Masr closed and fined its editor-in-chief, Lina Attalah, 3 million Egyptian pounds, the maximum penalty for operating a website without a licence. Security officers detained Attalah for several hours and released her after the outlet paid the fine. The court also ordered the seizure of Mada Masr’s equipment. The outlet says it will appeal the closure. Attalah’s defence team said the judge rejected its procedural requests, appointed a lawyer over Attalah’s objection and proceeded despite protests. Mada Masr says it applied for a licence in 2018 and that its latest application has gone unanswered since 2023. Authorities have blocked access to its website inside Egypt since 2017. Mada Masr has faced other legal cases. In September, authorities arrested six journalists from fact-checking platform Matsadaash. Prosecutors extended those journalists’ pretrial detention by 15 days on Oct. 27. After her release, Attalah also learned that she had received a one-year sentence in absentia in a separate 2024 case. A hearing to challenge that conviction is scheduled for Nov. 11.
world.image_alt: Egyptian court orders independent outlet Mada Masr closed, fines editor

world.title: Chinese sponsors drop Real Madrid star Mbappé over Mao remark
world.summary: Three Chinese companies ended sponsorship deals with France and Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappé on Oct. 27 after a clip circulated in which he appeared to call Mao Zedong a Chinese dictator; China’s state broadcaster also suspended La Liga match coverage and removed advertisements featuring him. The companies were be
world.content: Three Chinese companies ended sponsorship deals with France and Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappé on Oct. 27 after a clip circulated in which he appeared to call Mao Zedong a Chinese dictator; China’s state broadcaster also suspended La Liga match coverage and removed advertisements featuring him. The companies were beverage maker Dongpeng, dairy producer Mengniu and cheesemaker Milkground. The clip showed Mbappé discussing an internet meme that placed his face on Mao’s body. Reuters said it could not authenticate the video; the interview was reportedly filmed in April for the French online program The Bridge. Mbappé apologized in French, Mandarin and English, saying his comment was ill-judged and that he respected Chinese people and their history. Mao, who founded the People’s Republic of China and led it from 1949 until his death in 1976, remains a revered and politically sensitive figure. China’s ruling Communist Party acknowledges mistakes under his leadership but says his achievements outweighed them. China Media Group said it would consider Mbappé’s apology but judge his future actions.
world.image_alt: Chinese sponsors drop Real Madrid star Mbappé over Mao remark

world.title: Serbia’s student-backed list wins majority, ending Vučić’s 14-year rule
world.summary: Serbia’s opposition Student List, a slate backed by a leaderless student movement, is projected to win 140 of 250 parliamentary seats after the Oct. 25 election, defeating the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) of former president Aleksandar Vučić. Vučić conceded after the vote; he had resigned the presidency last month t
world.content: Serbia’s opposition Student List, a slate backed by a leaderless student movement, is projected to win 140 of 250 parliamentary seats after the Oct. 25 election, defeating the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) of former president Aleksandar Vučić. Vučić conceded after the vote; he had resigned the presidency last month to lead the SNS ticket. Preliminary figures put the Student List at about 53% of the vote and the SNS at 39%, with results still awaiting certification. The win follows nearly two years of protests sparked by the November 2024 collapse of a railway-station canopy in Novi Sad that killed 16 people. Students demanded accountability and an end to corruption, then broadened their campaign to include the rule of law and functioning public institutions. The Student List’s candidates have little governing experience, and its politically diverse supporters have not settled divisive foreign-policy questions. Serbia’s election process allows appeals and possible reruns at polling stations before results are finalized and a new parliament convenes. Lawmakers then have 90 days to form a government. Vučić’s resignation also requires a separate presidential election, and a year-end budget must be passed.
world.image_alt: Serbia’s student-backed list wins majority, ending Vučić’s 14-year rule

world.title: U.S. costs for Iran war reach $47.1 billion, with renewed strikes possible
world.summary: U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) estimates the military has spent $47.1 billion on the Iran war through Oct. 16, more than 25% above the $37.5 billion figure Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth gave Congress in July. The estimate includes about $29 billion to replace expended munitions, $6.1 billion for lost equipment and $11
world.content: U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) estimates the military has spent $47.1 billion on the Iran war through Oct. 16, more than 25% above the $37.5 billion figure Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth gave Congress in July. The estimate includes about $29 billion to replace expended munitions, $6.1 billion for lost equipment and $11.9 billion in other incremental costs. The tally does not include the cost of repairing U.S. bases damaged by Iranian missile and drone attacks. The war’s effect on global energy prices has weighed on support for Republican candidates and President Donald Trump’s approval ratings before the Nov. 3 midterm elections, which will decide control of Congress. Trump launched the war with Israel in February and later imposed a naval blockade on Iran; he has left open the possibility of resuming combat after the election. U.S. officials say the Pentagon is preparing for renewed heavy fighting if ordered, while Trump has also said Iran could agree to a deal.
world.image_alt: U.S. costs for Iran war reach $47.1 billion, with renewed strikes possible

world.title: King Charles says Commonwealth leaders will discuss slavery’s legacy at summit
world.summary: King Charles III said on Oct. 27 that Commonwealth leaders would discuss slavery’s legacy at their upcoming summit, after beginning a nine-day Caribbean tour in the Bahamas. At a youth rally in Nassau, he called it “only right” to acknowledge the suffering and injustices of the past, but did not apologize for Britain’s
world.content: King Charles III said on Oct. 27 that Commonwealth leaders would discuss slavery’s legacy at their upcoming summit, after beginning a nine-day Caribbean tour in the Bahamas. At a youth rally in Nassau, he called it “only right” to acknowledge the suffering and injustices of the past, but did not apologize for Britain’s role in the slave trade. Caribbean governments and campaigners are pressing Britain for a formal apology and reparations, while the British government has ruled out both. Guyana’s president, Mohamed Irfaan Ali, said an apology should follow the king’s acknowledgment. UK Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds called reparations an unreasonable request but said Britain should be able to discuss its history. Charles is due to visit Guyana and then attend the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda with Queen Camilla. The Nov. 1-4 summit is expected to address reparations alongside climate resilience, trade and investment. Charles also noted that 90% of the Bahamas’ land lies below two metres.
world.image_alt: King Charles says Commonwealth leaders will discuss slavery’s legacy at summit

business.title: Australia inflation hits 4.3%, putting fifth 2026 rate hike in view
business.summary: Australia’s annual inflation rate rose to 4.3% in September from 4% in August, increasing expectations that the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) will lift interest rates for a fifth time this year. The consumer price index (CPI) rose 0.8% over the month, while annual underlying inflation, measured by the trimmed mean, r
business.content: Australia’s annual inflation rate rose to 4.3% in September from 4% in August, increasing expectations that the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) will lift interest rates for a fifth time this year. The consumer price index (CPI) rose 0.8% over the month, while annual underlying inflation, measured by the trimmed mean, reached 3.6%. The RBA’s cash rate is already 4.6%, its highest level in 15 years, after four increases in 2026. Housing costs rose 5.2% over the year and were the largest contributor to inflation; transport costs also rose as fuel prices climbed. RBA Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said inflation was “too high,” while Treasurer Jim Chalmers pointed to high oil prices and the Middle East war. The RBA board meets next week and is due to announce its rate decision on Tuesday, November 3, alongside updated economic forecasts.
business.image_alt: Australia inflation hits 4.3%, putting fifth 2026 rate hike in view

business.title: Residential cruise operator halts voyage, leaves 203 passengers in Cambodia
business.summary: Villa Vie Residences suspended the voyage of its residential cruise ship, the Odyssey, in Sihanoukville, Cambodia, ordering 203 passengers to disembark after monthly fuel costs per cabin rose from about $1,800 to an estimated $6,000-$8,000 in parts of Asia. The ship also had 156 crew members aboard; their status was un
business.content: Villa Vie Residences suspended the voyage of its residential cruise ship, the Odyssey, in Sihanoukville, Cambodia, ordering 203 passengers to disembark after monthly fuel costs per cabin rose from about $1,800 to an estimated $6,000-$8,000 in parts of Asia. The ship also had 156 crew members aboard; their status was unclear. The operator said slowing the itinerary and spending more time in port had failed to offset the cost increase, and passing the full increase on to residents was not realistic. The Odyssey had been on a planned 3½-year global voyage after leaving Belfast in October 2024. Villa Vie said it was working to support residents, crew and employees while pursuing restructuring and recapitalization over the next 60 days. It warned that no outcome was assured and said no financing or transaction had been finalized.
business.image_alt: Residential cruise operator halts voyage, leaves 203 passengers in Cambodia

business.title: Deutsche Bank posts €2.63 billion third-quarter pretax profit
business.summary: Deutsche Bank reported third-quarter pretax profit of €2.63 billion, up 8% from a year earlier, as revenue rose 4% to €8.34 billion. Net profit was about €1.9 billion, including €1.59 billion attributable to shareholders. Pretax profit and shareholder earnings exceeded analysts’ forecasts of €2.39 billion and €1.44 bil
business.content: Deutsche Bank reported third-quarter pretax profit of €2.63 billion, up 8% from a year earlier, as revenue rose 4% to €8.34 billion. Net profit was about €1.9 billion, including €1.59 billion attributable to shareholders. Pretax profit and shareholder earnings exceeded analysts’ forecasts of €2.39 billion and €1.44 billion, respectively. The corporate bank was the strongest contributor, with pretax profit up 11% to €743 million. Investment-bank pretax profit rose 12% to about €1 billion despite a 2% decline in revenue, helped by lower credit-risk provisions and lower costs. Chief Executive Christian Sewing said the bank expects full-year 2026 revenue to exceed its roughly €33 billion target. Deutsche Bank also reported a 10.6% return on equity for the quarter, compared with its goal of more than 13% for 2028.
business.image_alt: Deutsche Bank posts €2.63 billion third-quarter pretax profit

business.title: Apple foldable-phone hinge supplier Fine M-Tec denies role in screen failures
business.summary: Fine M-Tec, a South Korean maker of hinge plates reported to supply Apple’s first foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo, denied that its components caused screen failures and said it is considering legal action over accusations made without objective verification. Some owners of Apple’s $1,999 foldable phone say its inner di
business.content: Fine M-Tec, a South Korean maker of hinge plates reported to supply Apple’s first foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo, denied that its components caused screen failures and said it is considering legal action over accusations made without objective verification. Some owners of Apple’s $1,999 foldable phone say its inner display cracked or developed lines soon after use. Apple has acknowledged an issue affecting a “small number” of units and directs customers with display problems to AppleCare for replacement; it has not publicly identified a cause or disclosed how many units are affected. Repair firm iFixit has suggested that a hinge support could press against the inner screen, but that remains a theory, not a confirmed cause. Claims circulating on Chinese social media that Apple lowered quality-inspection standards to speed production have not been independently verified, and Apple has not confirmed that its procedures changed. Apple plans to launch the Duo in 28 additional markets on October 30.
business.image_alt: Apple foldable-phone hinge supplier Fine M-Tec denies role in screen failures

business.title: Boeing delays 737 output target as cash-flow goals slip to 2029
business.summary: Boeing shares fell 10.7% Tuesday after the U.S. aircraft maker reported a third-quarter adjusted loss of 34 cents a share and said it would take longer to raise 737 MAX production and reach its cash-flow targets. Revenue rose 4% to $24.2 billion and free cash flow was $464 million, but Boeing said it must stabilize pro
business.content: Boeing shares fell 10.7% Tuesday after the U.S. aircraft maker reported a third-quarter adjusted loss of 34 cents a share and said it would take longer to raise 737 MAX production and reach its cash-flow targets. Revenue rose 4% to $24.2 billion and free cash flow was $464 million, but Boeing said it must stabilize production at 47 planes a month before increasing output to 52. It does not expect to reach that rate until the second half of 2027. Boeing also said it would miss its goal of delivering 500 737s in 2026 and now expects to reach annual free cash flow of $10 billion in 2029. Chief Executive Kelly Ortberg cited the need for more predictable wing production and fuselage manufacturing in Kansas. The company delivered 161 commercial aircraft in the third quarter, just one more than a year earlier.
business.image_alt: Boeing delays 737 output target as cash-flow goals slip to 2029

business.title: ByteDance founder Zhang Yiming regains China’s richest-person title on AI gains
business.summary: ByteDance founder Zhang Yiming regained the top spot on China’s rich list with an estimated fortune of nearly $100 billion, up 43% from a year earlier, as the company expanded its artificial-intelligence business. Hurun Research Institute chairman Rupert Hoogewerf attributed almost all of Zhang’s increase to AI; ByteDa
business.content: ByteDance founder Zhang Yiming regained the top spot on China’s rich list with an estimated fortune of nearly $100 billion, up 43% from a year earlier, as the company expanded its artificial-intelligence business. Hurun Research Institute chairman Rupert Hoogewerf attributed almost all of Zhang’s increase to AI; ByteDance’s Doubao assistant is China’s most-used AI assistant, Hurun said. AI, semiconductor and robotics fortunes rose in the ranking, while wealth in consumer industries, property and traditional manufacturing declined. China’s economy grew 4.5% year over year in the third quarter, supported by exports, as weak domestic demand and a prolonged property downturn weighed on growth. Hurun released the list on Oct. 27, based on fortunes measured as of Sept. 1.
business.image_alt: ByteDance founder Zhang Yiming regains China’s richest-person title on AI gains

business.title: UK budget scraps gas standing charges as borrowing costs rise
business.summary: The Treasury confirmed Wednesday that fixed standing charges on gas bills will be removed from 2027, affecting about 23 million homes. It estimates three-fifths of households will save an average £45 a year, although higher gas-use charges will offset the savings for some and leave high users paying more. UK Chancellor
business.content: The Treasury confirmed Wednesday that fixed standing charges on gas bills will be removed from 2027, affecting about 23 million homes. It estimates three-fifths of households will save an average £45 a year, although higher gas-use charges will offset the savings for some and leave high users paying more. UK Chancellor John Healey was due to deliver his first budget statement in Parliament later Wednesday. Healey is also expected to extend the fuel-duty freeze and raise the minimum wage by 3.9%, while the government has announced import-tariff cuts on more than 100 products and changes to carers’ and parental pay. A planned £20.4 billion in additional capital for public lenders is intended to support projects in energy, defence and artificial intelligence. The government’s £23.6 billion fiscal headroom in March may have fallen to about £12 billion, while debt-service costs have risen and UK public debt has passed £3 trillion. The fiscal watchdog will release updated forecasts alongside the budget; Healey has said he will stick to the government’s fiscal rules.
business.image_alt: UK budget scraps gas standing charges as borrowing costs rise

business.title: Chinese brands end Mbappé deals as La Liga seeks to protect China TV business
business.summary: Three Chinese companies have ended endorsement agreements with Kylian Mbappé, the France captain and Real Madrid forward, after a video circulated in which he appeared to describe Mao Zedong as a Chinese dictator. Beverage maker Dongpeng, dairy producer Mengniu and cheesemaker Milkground each announced they had ended c
business.content: Three Chinese companies have ended endorsement agreements with Kylian Mbappé, the France captain and Real Madrid forward, after a video circulated in which he appeared to describe Mao Zedong as a Chinese dictator. Beverage maker Dongpeng, dairy producer Mengniu and cheesemaker Milkground each announced they had ended cooperation with him. Their campaigns had featured Mbappé’s image on products and in advertising in China. China Media Group said it had suspended broadcasts of La Liga matches and removed Mbappé advertisements. La Liga apologized to Chinese fans and said it was working with Chinese partners on a communications protocol for players and clubs. The effect on Mbappé’s other global deals remains unclear. Shares in Swiss shoemaker On fell more than 4% in early trading on Oct. 27. On and Dior reportedly removed Chinese promotional content featuring Mbappé; neither company had announced it was ending its global deal with him. As of Oct. 28, CNBC said it could not independently confirm whether La Liga broadcasts had resumed or access to Mbappé’s social accounts had been restored.
business.image_alt: Chinese brands end Mbappé deals as La Liga seeks to protect China TV business

science.title: Andrews Glacier thinned more than 12 feet after record-low snow in 2026
science.summary: Colorado’s Rocky Mountain glaciers thinned sharply in 2026 after record-low snowpack and record summer heat exposed their ice. Andrews Glacier lost more than 12 feet, Arapaho nearly 10 feet and Isabelle about 6.5 feet; St. Mary’s Glacier melted completely in September. The three glaciers’ thinning rates were twice thos
science.content: Colorado’s Rocky Mountain glaciers thinned sharply in 2026 after record-low snowpack and record summer heat exposed their ice. Andrews Glacier lost more than 12 feet, Arapaho nearly 10 feet and Isabelle about 6.5 feet; St. Mary’s Glacier melted completely in September. The three glaciers’ thinning rates were twice those of the previous five years. A separate inventory of 1,331 western glaciers found their combined area had shrunk 35% and volume 33% since the 1950s, with nearly one-quarter of glaciers recorded in the mid-20th century now gone. Colorado State University glaciologist Dan McGrath said Colorado’s remaining glaciers could disappear within 20 years at the current rate.
science.image_alt: Andrews Glacier thinned more than 12 feet after record-low snow in 2026

science.title: Ancient fossils and genomes reveal human ties across Eurasia
science.summary: Researchers identified five Denisovan fossils in southwest China, while genomes from three Gravettian people who lived about 30,000 years ago showed links between western and eastern European groups. The findings came from separate research projects. The Chinese fossils include the first confirmed Denisovan radius, a f
science.content: Researchers identified five Denisovan fossils in southwest China, while genomes from three Gravettian people who lived about 30,000 years ago showed links between western and eastern European groups. The findings came from separate research projects. The Chinese fossils include the first confirmed Denisovan radius, a forearm bone with traits resembling those of both Neanderthals and modern humans. In the European study, a woman whose bones were found in Isturitz Cave in southwestern France carried ancestry linked to eastern and central Europe. Researchers dated the gene flow to about 31,500 to 32,500 years ago.
science.image_alt: Ancient fossils and genomes reveal human ties across Eurasia

science.title: Lancet study finds heat exposure cost 573 billion work hours in 2025
science.summary: A Lancet Countdown study found that heat exposure cost the world 573 billion potential work hours in 2025, with lost productivity valued at $1.07 trillion. Drought affected more than half of global land for at least a month that year. The losses fell hardest on low- and middle-income countries and outdoor sectors such
science.content: A Lancet Countdown study found that heat exposure cost the world 573 billion potential work hours in 2025, with lost productivity valued at $1.07 trillion. Drought affected more than half of global land for at least a month that year. The losses fell hardest on low- and middle-income countries and outdoor sectors such as agriculture and construction. The report, compiled by 146 researchers from 30 countries, calls for climate change to be treated as a global health emergency and for a coordinated response centered on health. It found that 56 World Health Organization member states had adapted health or early-warning systems, while 84% of climate-health research funding went to researchers in wealthy countries.
science.image_alt: Lancet study finds heat exposure cost 573 billion work hours in 2025

science.title: Studies examine dementia resilience, diet and aspirin risks
science.summary: Three separate studies examined brain aging and dementia. Researchers at the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience found immature neurons in brain tissue from people with Alzheimer’s pathology who remained cognitively healthy, people with Alzheimer’s dementia and people without detectable pathology. In the cognitively
science.content: Three separate studies examined brain aging and dementia. Researchers at the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience found immature neurons in brain tissue from people with Alzheimer’s pathology who remained cognitively healthy, people with Alzheimer’s dementia and people without detectable pathology. In the cognitively resilient group, the cells showed activity patterns associated with survival, along with lower inflammation and cell-death signals, but the study did not establish what the cells do. A separate genetic analysis of more than 13,500 participants in the ASPREE aspirin trial found fewer dementia diagnoses but more major bleeding among low-dose aspirin recipients in the highest fifth of a platelet-related genetic score. A small peanut trial also found improved insulin responsiveness in memory-related brain regions after daily peanut consumption.
science.image_alt: Studies examine dementia resilience, diet and aspirin risks

science.title: Arizona’s Chiricahua becomes U.S. national park after congressional act
science.summary: Chiricahua in southeastern Arizona became the United States’ 64th national park in October, after Congress passed a bill and President Donald J. Trump signed it into law. The 12,000-acre area had been a national monument for more than a century. The park’s rock spires and canyons formed as erosion wore away volcanic de
science.content: Chiricahua in southeastern Arizona became the United States’ 64th national park in October, after Congress passed a bill and President Donald J. Trump signed it into law. The 12,000-acre area had been a national monument for more than a century. The park’s rock spires and canyons formed as erosion wore away volcanic deposits left by eruptions about 27 million years ago. The new designation covers a landscape with a long human history and is expected to draw more visitors, who tend to stay overnight more often at national parks than at monuments.
science.image_alt: Arizona’s Chiricahua becomes U.S. national park after congressional act

science.title: Record king tides flood US coasts as El Niño raises winter risks
science.summary: Record-breaking king tides flooded coastal communities in Southern California and Florida this week, with water levels setting records at tide gauges in Los Angeles Harbor, La Jolla and Santa Barbara. Several factors combined to produce the high water levels: the full moon’s tidal pull, the expansion of unusually warm
science.content: Record-breaking king tides flooded coastal communities in Southern California and Florida this week, with water levels setting records at tide gauges in Los Angeles Harbor, La Jolla and Santa Barbara. Several factors combined to produce the high water levels: the full moon’s tidal pull, the expansion of unusually warm ocean water, an El Niño pattern and a Kelvin wave carrying warm water toward the California coast. Higher baseline sea levels and strong onshore winds have added to the flooding in some areas. Coastal flood warnings in Southern California were set to remain in effect through Thursday, Oct. 29, while forecasters expect another round of especially high tides later in the year as king tides and El Niño conditions coincide. California’s next statewide king tide periods are forecast for Nov. 24-26, Dec. 23-25 and Jan. 21-22; scientists say winter storms and rain could worsen flooding during those periods.
science.image_alt: Record king tides flood US coasts as El Niño raises winter risks

science.title: Brazilian President Lula wins reelection, keeping Amazon protections on agenda
science.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won re-election on Oct. 25 with 51.79% of the vote, defeating Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and securing another four-year term. Lula has pledged to end deforestation by 2030. Environmental groups and scientists welcomed continued Amazon protection but warned that a conservative
science.content: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won re-election on Oct. 25 with 51.79% of the vote, defeating Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and securing another four-year term. Lula has pledged to end deforestation by 2030. Environmental groups and scientists welcomed continued Amazon protection but warned that a conservative-leaning National Congress could impede new safeguards. Lula’s support for offshore oil exploration near the Amazon also conflicts with that agenda. Flávio Bolsonaro said he would seek to annul the result. Brazil’s electoral court is due to certify it by Dec. 18, and he would need evidence sufficient to overturn the winning margin. The next round of U.N. climate talks is scheduled to begin Nov. 9 in Türkiye, after Brazil hosted COP30 in Belém in 2025.
science.image_alt: Brazilian President Lula wins reelection, keeping Amazon protections on agenda

science.title: Rare Nanotyrannus dinosaur skeleton sells for $47.3 million in New York
science.summary: A rare Nanotyrannus skeleton known as Jodi sold for $47.3 million at Sotheby’s in New York on Tuesday, far above its estimate of $6 million to $9 million. It became the second-most expensive dinosaur fossil sold at auction. Discovered in Montana in 2019, Jodi is one of only three substantial Nanotyrannus skeletons know
science.content: A rare Nanotyrannus skeleton known as Jodi sold for $47.3 million at Sotheby’s in New York on Tuesday, far above its estimate of $6 million to $9 million. It became the second-most expensive dinosaur fossil sold at auction. Discovered in Montana in 2019, Jodi is one of only three substantial Nanotyrannus skeletons known and belonged to an adult animal that lived about 67 million years ago. Thomas R. Holtz Jr., a vertebrate paleontology lecturer at the University of Maryland, warned that privately owned fossils can become inaccessible to researchers and the public. Researchers confirmed last year that Nanotyrannus was distinct from Tyrannosaurus rex, rather than a juvenile T. rex, ending a decades-long debate. The winning bidder has not been publicly identified.
science.image_alt: Rare Nanotyrannus dinosaur skeleton sells for $47.3 million in New York

sports.title: WNBA moves Finals Game 6 to 12:30 p.m. over Atlanta arena scheduling conflict
sports.summary: The WNBA moved Game 6 of the Finals between the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries to 12:30 p.m. ET Thursday, Oct. 29, at Atlanta’s State Farm Arena because the Atlanta Hawks have a home game against the Cleveland Cavaliers there that night. Golden State leads the best-of-seven series 3-2 and can clinch its first
sports.content: The WNBA moved Game 6 of the Finals between the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries to 12:30 p.m. ET Thursday, Oct. 29, at Atlanta’s State Farm Arena because the Atlanta Hawks have a home game against the Cleveland Cavaliers there that night. Golden State leads the best-of-seven series 3-2 and can clinch its first championship; Atlanta needs a win to force Game 7 in San Francisco. The Hawks-Cavaliers game remains at 8 p.m. Both NBA teams play Wednesday, ruling out an earlier tipoff Thursday, though the leagues explored ways to keep the Finals game in prime time. In an open letter Tuesday, Dream ownership said it raised the venue conflict two months ago and repeated its concerns during the playoffs. The team normally plays at 3,500-seat Gateway Center Arena but chose the 17,000-seat State Farm Arena to accommodate more Finals fans. Ownership said a midday weekday game was not its preferred outcome. The WNBA cited sellout crowds for Games 3 and 4 as a reason to give more fans access to Game 6. If Atlanta wins, Game 7 is scheduled for Saturday at Chase Center.

sports.content: Minnesota Timberwolves guard Anthony Edwards is scheduled to undergo arthroscopic surgery on his right knee Thursday and could miss up to two months, leaving the 3-1 team without its leading scorer early in the season. The procedure addresses a knee problem that resurfaced during the opening games after troubling him last season; a more precise recovery timetable is expected after surgery. Edwards averaged 33.3 points through four games, including 47 in Monday’s overtime loss to Cleveland, and set a Timberwolves record with 133 points in the first four games. His absence puts more offensive responsibility on newly acquired point guard LaMelo Ball and other teammates. A two-month absence would leave Edwards below the NBA’s 65-game threshold for major postseason awards.

sports.content: India beat New Zealand by six wickets in Wellington on Tuesday, October 27, to clinch their five-match Twenty20 international series with a 3-0 lead. Chasing 199, India reached 199-4 in 13.2 overs as opener Abhishek Sharma struck 113 from 38 balls, reaching his century off 35, and fellow opener Vaibhav Sooryavanshi made 45 from 19. The pair added 133 in just over seven overs, and India’s 118 without loss in the six-over powerplay set a men’s T20 international record. New Zealand posted 198-3, led by Daryl Mitchell’s unbeaten 89 from 52 balls. Abhishek’s 11 sixes took his 2026 total to 85, surpassing Rohit Sharma’s previous calendar-year record of 80 by a batter from a Full Member nation. India head to Auckland for the fourth match on October 30 and Hamilton for the finale on November 1. Mitchell said New Zealand would regroup, while captain Mitchell Santner noted that Eden Park could be smaller all round.

sports.content: Liverpool host Chelsea at Anfield on Wednesday in the Carabao Cup fourth round, with a quarter-final place at stake and former Liverpool midfielder Xabi Alonso returning as Chelsea manager. Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola and Alonso, childhood friends from the Basque Country, now meet as opposing coaches. Liverpool have won their last four matches, while Chelsea are seeking a response to Saturday’s 2-0 home defeat by Tottenham. Chelsea will be without forward João Pedro, who is expected to miss several weeks with a thigh injury, and suspended attacker Cole Palmer. Alonso could turn to Danny Welbeck or give summer signing Emmanuel Emegha his first appearance after his return to training following injury. Liverpool are considering rotating their squad, with Florian Wirtz a fitness doubt and several defenders and midfielders unavailable. Young players including Trey Nyoni and Rio Ngumoha are among the options. The match kicks off at 8pm UK time, with the Carabao Cup quarter-final draw scheduled to follow. Liverpool last beat Chelsea in the competition’s 2024 final and won both clubs’ two most recent final meetings.

sports.content: Sri Lanka beat Pakistan by eight wickets in Lahore on Tuesday to qualify for Saturday’s one-day international tri-series final and eliminate England with a league match still to play. Left-arm fast bowler Dilshan Madushanka took a career-best five wickets for 34 runs as Pakistan were dismissed for 110 in 25.3 overs. Sri Lanka reached 114-2 in 18.1 overs, with Kamindu Mendis unbeaten on 62. Sri Lanka lost the tournament opener to Pakistan by 37 runs before chasing 430 against England for the second-highest successful chase in one-day international history. Pakistan had already secured a place in the final with three wins, including a one-wicket victory over England on Sunday. England’s three defeats left them unable to qualify. Sri Lanka and England are scheduled to meet on Thursday, October 29, in a match that can no longer change the finalists. Pakistan and Sri Lanka will meet again in the final at Lahore’s Gaddafi Stadium on Saturday, October 31.

sports.content: The Indianapolis Colts traded eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder, then sent three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers for a 2027 fourth-round pick on Tuesday, Oct. 27. Nelson joins the defending Super Bowl champions; Buckner returns to the team that drafted him seventh overall in 2016. Seattle is adding help for its ground game, while San Francisco is reinforcing an injury-depleted defensive line as it pursues a playoff berth. The Colts, now 2-5 after three straight losses, made the trades after firing general manager Chris Ballard. They gained three draft picks but still lack a 2027 first-round selection, having sent it to the New York Jets in the trade for cornerback Sauce Gardner. The NFL trade deadline is Nov. 10. Running back Jonathan Taylor and receiver Josh Downs are among the players discussed as possible trade candidates.

sports.content: The Minnesota Vikings enter NFL Week 8 at 6-0 as the league’s only unbeaten team after the Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers each lost their first game in Week 7. Minnesota’s 16-10 win over Indianapolis kept the Vikings atop one power ranking. They play Sunday at Detroit, followed by games against Buffalo, Green Bay and San Francisco. Week 8 opens Thursday, Oct. 29, with Carolina at Green Bay and closes Monday, Nov. 2, when Chicago visits Seattle; Sunday’s slate includes Ravens-Bills and Chiefs-Broncos. Houston, New Orleans, the New York Giants and San Francisco have byes. Baltimore’s Lamar Jackson returned to practice last week as he recovers from an ankle injury.

sports.content: Fourth-tier Fleetwood Town beat Premier League champions Arsenal 5-3 on penalties on Tuesday, October 27, after a 1-1 draw to reach the Carabao Cup quarter-finals for the first time. Aaron Loupalo-Bi put Fleetwood ahead in the 21st minute; Arsenal’s Viktor Gyökeres equalised five minutes after half-time, and 16-year-old Arsenal winger Max Dowman was sent off late in the match. Fleetwood goalkeeper Jay Lynch saved Arsenal’s Bruno Guimarães’s penalty before 19-year-old defender Conor Haughey converted the decisive kick. Fleetwood were 18th in League Two and 84 places below Arsenal in the English football pyramid. Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta made nine changes from Saturday’s win over Everton ahead of Sunday’s Premier League trip to Liverpool. The visitors controlled much of the game but could not find a second goal. Fleetwood will learn their quarter-final opponent after Wednesday’s Chelsea-Liverpool match, with the last eight scheduled for December. Arsenal’s next match is against Liverpool this weekend.
